Smooth curves observed on a common grid into a functional data object

Source: R/funsmooth.R
funSmooth.Rd

Fits a penalised B-spline smoother (fda::smooth.basis()) to curves observed on the same grid r, for example summary functions (K, L, g) estimated for several samples. The table must contain one column with the grid (r_value by default) and one numeric column per curve.

Usage

funSmooth(
  df,
  norder = 6,
  Lfdobj = 4,
  r_col = NULL,
  centered = FALSE,
  nbasis = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  rangeval = NULL,
  fun_type = c("none", "L", "K", "g"),
  unit = "pixel",
  to_micron = FALSE,
  mpp = NULL,
  magnif = NULL,
  mpp_ref = 0.25,
  mag_ref = 40,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data.frame or data.table with the grid column and one numeric column per curve.

norder

Spline order (norder in fda). Must be a positive integer.

Lfdobj

Order of the derivative used in the roughness penalty (Lfdobj of fda::fdPar()): a non-negative integer smaller than norder, or an Lfd object.

r_col

Name of the grid column. NULL (default) means "r_value".

centered

If TRUE, r is subtracted from every curve before smoothing (L(r) - r).

nbasis

Number of basis functions. If NULL, min(30, max(norder + 1, floor(length(r) / 4))). If it is not smaller than the number of grid points it is reduced to max(norder + 1, length(r) - 1). Ignored when breaks is given.

breaks

Optional knot vector (strictly increasing, from rangeval[1] to rangeval[2]); then nbasis = length(breaks) + norder - 2.

lambda

Smoothing penalty, a non-negative number. If NULL, it is chosen by generalised cross-validation (GCV), with the same basis and penalty used for the fit.

rangeval

Range of the basis, c(min, max). If NULL, range(r). Must contain all the grid values.

fun_type

Summary function in the curves: "none" (default), "L", "K" or "g". Used for the labels and to rescale the values when converting units.

unit

Unit of the r column, a single string (default "pixel").

to_micron

If TRUE, converts from pixels to microns (requires unit = "pixel" and one of mpp or magnif).

mpp

Microns per pixel.

magnif

Magnification of the coordinates (e.g. 20 or 40), alternative to mpp.

mpp_ref, mag_ref

Microns per pixel at a reference magnification, used with magnif. Default: 0.25 micron/pixel at 40x.

verbose

If TRUE, prints messages on the choices made.

...

Other arguments passed to fda::smooth.basis() (e.g. wtvec).

Value

An object of class spafun_fd, a list with:

  • fd: the smoothed curves, an fd object (one replicate per curve, named after the curve columns);

  • fdPar: the fdPar object actually used for the fit;

  • basis: the B-spline basis;

  • mat: the matrix of curves (converted and centred, as smoothed);

  • r: the grid (converted);

  • centered: whether r was subtracted from the curves;

  • fun_type: the summary function;

  • unit: the unit of r in the result;

  • settings: list with the smoothing parameters actually used (norder, Lfdobj as derivative order, nbasis, breaks, rangeval, lambda, lambda_method "gcv" or "user", df of the GCV fit, fallback) and the unit conversion (unit_in, to_micron, mpp).

See print.spafun_fd() for the methods.

Details

If smooth.basis() fails, a second attempt is made with a second derivative penalty (Lfdobj = 2) and lambda = max(lambda, 1e-4), with a warning; the settings actually used are stored in the result.

Units: unit is the unit of the r column (free text, e.g. "pixel" or "micron"). With to_micron = TRUE (only from "pixel") the grid is multiplied by the microns per pixel mpp, given directly or as mpp = mpp_ref * mag_ref / magnif. The curve values are rescaled according to fun_type: L has the unit of a length (* mpp), K of an area (* mpp^2), g and "none" are left unchanged. rangeval and breaks are in the unit of the r column and are converted with it.

See also

fda::smooth.basis(), fda::pca.fd()

Examples

# three noisy curves observed on the same grid
set.seed(1)
r <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 50)
curves <- data.frame(
  r_value = r,
  A = sin(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1),
  B = cos(2 * pi * r) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1),
  C = r^2 + rnorm(50, sd = 0.1)
)

res <- funSmooth(curves, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: lambda reduced to 259.568955954505 to prevent overflow
#> Warning: lambda reduced to 259.568955954505 to prevent overflow
#> Warning: lambda reduced to 259.568955954505 to prevent overflow
res
#> <spafun_fd> 3 curves
#>   r:          [0, 1] pixel, 50 points
#>   function:   Value
#>   centered:   no
#>   basis:      B-spline, order 6, 12 basis functions
#>   penalty:    derivative 4, lambda = 5.31e-08 (GCV, df = 6.35)
plot(res)
#> Ignoring unknown labels:
#> • colour : "Group"


# grid column with another name, fixed number of basis functions and a
# stronger penalty
names(curves)[1] <- "dist"
res2 <- funSmooth(curves, r_col = "dist", nbasis = 10, lambda = 1e-3,
                  verbose = FALSE)

# the result can be used directly in fda, e.g. for a functional PCA
pca <- fda::pca.fd(res2$fd, nharm = 2, harmfdPar = res2$fdPar)
pca$varprop
#> [1] 0.6767749 0.3232251

# L functions computed on coordinates in pixels at 40x, converted to
# microns (0.25 micron/pixel at 40x) and centred: L(r) - r
r_px <- seq(0, 200, length.out = 60)
L_px <- data.frame(r_value = r_px,
                   s1 = r_px + 5 * sin(r_px / 30),
                   s2 = r_px - 3 * sin(r_px / 40))
res_um <- funSmooth(L_px, fun_type = "L", centered = TRUE,
                    to_micron = TRUE, magnif = 40, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: GCV minimum on the border of the range: consider widening `dfRange`.
res_um$unit
#> [1] "micron"
range(res_um$r)
#> [1]  0 50
head(as.data.frame(res_um))
#>           r sample         value
#> 1 0.0000000     s1 -7.101904e-06
#> 2 0.8474576     s1  1.409508e-01
#> 3 1.6949153     s1  2.800923e-01
#> 4 2.5423729     s1  4.156588e-01
#> 5 3.3898305     s1  5.459278e-01
#> 6 4.2372881     s1  6.692379e-01
